top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) is a chemical design rule that lets small molecules direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins, including targets with no active site. It is reproduced widely, supported by ternary-complex structures, and already rooted in approved drugs through cereblon glues. It changes what chemists and clinicians can do more directly than the other proposals; attribution and the lack of an approved bifunctional degrader are acknowledged weaknesses. P002 follows because it keeps the degradation part, though its Crews and Handa cut omits Deshaies, ahead of base editing, which is chemically elegant but younger.
